title: Ajita's question (Sn 5)
hookLine: read it: what smothers the world? ignorance
tomorrow: so where does suffering come from? the next student asks.

cards: Snow overnight, and the whole street goes quiet: the cars are still there, the houses, the trees, just muffled under white. Fog on the highway does the same; the road hasn't gone anywhere, you just can't see it.
A new section of the Sutta Nipata begins here, the way to the far shore, and its first question, from the first of a group of students, is that riddle exactly.
A student named Ajita asks the Buddha: what is the world covered by? Why doesn't it shine?

teach.b: Ajita asks four things in one breath, and the Buddha answers each. The world is covered by ignorance, avijja: not seeing what's there. It doesn't shine because of greed and carelessness.
Craving is what smears it. Suffering is its great fear. Then Ajita asks about the streams of craving that run everywhere: what holds them back?
Mindfulness, the Buddha says, is the dam, and wisdom shuts them off. Notice the picture. The world isn't dark.
It's covered. Whatever shines is still underneath, the way the road is still under the fog. Now a neighbor.

teach.h: JOHN: THE LIGHT SHINETH IN DARKNESS.
teach.b: Christians read a line about light and darkness at the start of John's Gospel, in the King James words: "And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not."
Here's what the two share: the sense that what's real can be hidden, and that something can shine through what hides it. And here's an honest difference.

In John, the light is the Word, whom the Gospel says was with God and was God, coming into the world. In Ajita's answer, no light arrives from outside. The cover lifts as a person grows mindful and wise.
Two traditions, one old human question about darkness, two answers. Neither needs to become the other.
What smothers the world, for Ajita, is not seeing.

how: The Parayana, the way to the far shore, is read in Theravada study as a set of students' questions with the Buddha's short answers; teachers often take one question at a time and sit with it.

o: a king's riddle about where the sun goes at night
a student's question: what covers the world so it can't shine?
the first rule a teacher gave his students on a trip

s: in Ajita's answer, the world itself is dark and bad
the world is covered, not dark; whatever shines is still underneath.
John's Gospel and Ajita's answer both picture something real hidden by darkness
and they differ: in John the light is the Word coming into the world; for Ajita, mindfulness and wisdom lift the cover.
the Buddha says the cure for ignorance is to believe the right thing
he names mindfulness as the dam and wisdom as what shuts the streams: a way of seeing, not a creed to sign.

games.q: your roommate has been angry at a neighbor for weeks over a noise that turns out to be the building's pipes. what does Ajita's answer say was going on?
o: a cover of not-seeing; once it lifted, the neighbor was never the problem.
bad luck; the pipes were noisy, so anyone would have blamed the neighbor.
the roommate is a bad person, which is what ignorance really means.
games.why: the world is covered by ignorance, not seeing what's there. the anger grew under that cover; mindfulness is the dam, and wisdom lifts it.

practice: Turn toward the nearest window or lamp and let your eyes rest on the light, softly, not staring.
Then let your gaze drift slowly around the room and find one thing that was there all along that you hadn't really seen today: a crack, a color, a shadow. Stay with it until the bell.

wordCard.voice: Ajita's question: the first student's question on the way to the far shore. What covers the world? Ignorance, not seeing. Mindfulness is the dam; wisdom shuts the streams.

orig.note: Pali: ignorance, not-seeing; Sanskrit avidya. What the world is covered by.

carryVoice: For the foggy hours: what smothers the world is not seeing, and covers can lift. Day sixteen seventy-two, uncovered.

sources.ref: Sutta Nipata 5.2 (Ajitamanavapuccha, Ajita's question, in the Parayanavagga)

sources.q: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
